rules.body: Apply when a shared progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, and decoding can settle later. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without\nopening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file." File identity therefore cannot substitute for visit or attempt identity.

Register the panel listener before starting a source that can emit synchronously. TASK: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later\npacket arrives. Restore the initial progress update". README.md: "start may emit cached\npackets synchronously". The original ordering in src/Workflow.java is: "env.call(\"start\",file.token);subscription=((Number)env.call(\"listen\",file.token,callback)).intValue();"

Assign packet arrival order before invoking decode, and allow publication only if that packet is newer than the last displayed packet for its originating attempt. TASK: "Full\nprogress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the\ncurrent display backward." README.md: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Freshness must follow arrival order rather than decode completion or increasing byte counts.

Revoke a retired visit's packet admission and publication immediately, including while startup has not returned its cleanup capability. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." Check originating visit and attempt eligibility before decoding each subsequent packet and before publishing its result.

Keep audit settlement independent of display eligibility: an already-admitted decode retains its audit even if a newer frame displays or its visit retires. README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." src/Workflow.java: "Consumer<Object> deliver=frame->{ audit.accept(frame);view.accept(frame,order);};" TASK requires preserving "audit" behavior. Rejecting stale publication must not suppress the admitted packet's existing audit.

Associate cancellation and listener cleanup with the originating attempt, and recheck ownership after synchronous host callbacks before installing returned resources. README.md: "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;\nthat callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is\ninert." src/Workflow.java: "public void cancel(){if(aborted)return;aborted=true;stop.run();env.call(\"cancel\",file.token,number);}" Preserve idempotence and prevent an old continuation from replacing the active visit's resources.

Limit the repair to panel startup, ordering, and the lifecycle handling required by those changes. TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses." README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}\nunless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." README.md describes telemetry as "existing live delta observations" and says: "Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance." Do not apply panel startup or full-frame filtering changes indiscriminately to telemetry, or expand queue records.

Verify warm synchronous startup and ordinary streaming; reverse decode settlement with all admitted audits retained; and a newer frame whose loaded value decreases. Exercise multiple startup packets with synchronous hide, file switching, and same-file reopening before start returns. Verify delayed settlement after retirement or retry, cleanup callback reentry, repeated cancellation, and valid progress for the subsequent active visit. These checks follow README.md's statements that "Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order", "loaded values can decrease or reset", and callbacks "may synchronously select, hide or dispose". Also check the unchanged telemetry and queue behavior required by TASK and README.md.

limitations: These rules apply to the supplied synchronous host embedding; they do not establish thread safety or behavior under concurrent callbacks.
README.md states: "A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion are outside this embedding's model." Exception recovery is unspecified.
Frame structure is unspecified. Arrival freshness cannot depend on an assumed frame timestamp, sequence field, or increasing loaded value.
The supplied successful public examples cover only particular executions. Passing once does not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.
Experience, automatic contracts, and evaluation observations are guidance only; the rules below derive from TASK and supplied public source/documentation.
No files were modified and no runtime verification was performed for this extraction.
